metadata.title: Fills the Template, Doesn't Design the Deal.
metadata.subtitle: The LBO-Model Skill (Anthropic Skills)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude runs an Anthropic Skill like lbo-model, does it design the LBO model itself, the way an analyst building deal assumptions would, or does it just fill in an existing template's formulas and check them? Lands the carry-out that a Skill fills in and validates what's already there instead of designing it, which is why it can run on whatever LBO template you hand it, and never further than what that template and the file say.

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is lbo-model. The SKILL.md file inside it is the full instruction set — plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The actual pipeline lives in the file's Steps section. Claude reads each step and executes it, one at a time, in the order written. Linear — it doesn't branch unless a step tells it to.

Concretely, that means three things: it fills in the template's formulas, it validates the calculations against each other, and it checks the formatting against a professional standard. And because it reads the template's own structure first, it can do that on whatever LBO template you hand it — not just one fixed layout.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I want to fill in an LBO model template for a leveraged buyout deal. Read the lbo-model skill and walk me through what you will do before you do it. That last clause matters — asking Claude to explain first, before it runs, is what actually shows you the steps the file wrote for it.
